discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (2D materials, moire quantum matter)
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (PNAS 2011) predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees makes the electronic bands nearly flat, so electron interactions dominate kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group fabricated such devices with exquisite control and demonstrated correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in a pure-carbon system whose density is tuned by a gate electrode. This established twist angle as a new, continuously tunable parameter of quantum matter. The resulting field of moire materials has since delivered orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, Chern insulators, Wigner crystals and, recently, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted semiconductors and graphene. It turned van der Waals heterostructures into a programmable laboratory for strongly correlated physics. Hundreds of groups worldwide, including in India, now use it, and it has changed how experimental condensed-matter physics is done.
